landing.heroLede: Measure the site, build the estimate from a catalogue with ready prices — and send your client a link where they see everything and sign online.
landing.heroNote: Free: 2 projects — portal, signing, PDF and photos. No card required
landing.tradesNote: Catalogue and templates — for your trade
landing.problemSubtitle: Estimates in Excel or a notebook. Areas calculated on a scrap of paper. Receipts get lost. And when the client asks “can I see the detail?” — you build it all over again.
landing.bad1: Areas worked out on a scrap of paper — then copied into every line
landing.bad2: Estimates in Excel or a notebook; the client gets a photo of the page
landing.bad3: Receipts get lost, costs are tracked from memory
landing.bad4: What you actually earned on a job — only in your head
landing.good1: Measure once — tick that area into any estimate line
landing.good2: The client opens a link and signs online, no registration
landing.good3: Snap a sketch or a receipt — lines and measurements fill themselves in
landing.good4: Costs against income — your net profit per project, as a number
landing.featuresTitle: Majstr keeps it in one place
landing.featuresSubtitle: Measurements → estimate → client → money. One project, the whole picture: what you measured, what you priced, what the client approved and what you earned on it.
landing.feature1Text: Rooms, walls, sloped ceilings, built partitions, window reveals. Complex shapes come with a diagram showing exactly what to measure. Calculate once — tick it into any estimate line. Ceilings in five rooms — one line, not five.
landing.feature2Title: Take a photo — it fills itself in
landing.feature2Text: Sketch a room with dimensions and snap it — measurements are created. Photo of a shop receipt — items land in the estimate. Your price list in Excel — imported in a minute. You just review and confirm.
landing.feature3Title: Your client sees and signs online
landing.feature3Text: Send a link or a PDF. They open it on their phone, review the estimate line by line and sign — no registration, no messenger back-and-forth. You see the status: viewed, signed.
landing.feature4Text: Add material and labour costs — and see your net profit on every project. Not a rough guess, a number. It's immediately clear which job paid off and where you undercharged.
landing.stepsTitle: Three steps from request to signature
landing.step1Text: The catalogue fills itself with market prices — for tiling, electrical, plumbing or construction. Adjust the prices to yours; only you see them. Got a price list in Excel — import it in a minute.
landing.step2Text: Room by room: walls, ceiling, floor, partitions, reveals. Complex mansard shapes come with a diagram to guide you. Or just photograph your sketch with its dimensions — it gets recognised.
landing.step3Title: Build the estimate and send it
landing.step3Text: Take a ready template for a typical job, tick in the areas from your measurements — and send the client a link. They approve it online.
landing.finalText: Registration takes a couple of minutes. A catalogue of 1000+ works with prices and 120+ ready templates are already inside. Two projects free: portal, signing, PDF and photos.
landing.faqA1: The base plan is free: two projects with the client portal, online signing, PDF and photos. PRO is a paid subscription (monthly or yearly) that removes the project limit and adds photo recognition and estimate import. A free PRO trial is available to new users.
landing.faqQ2: Does the client need to register to sign an estimate?
landing.faqA2: No. The client opens a link on their phone, reviews the estimate line by line and signs online — no registration and no app.
landing.faqA3: Almost everything does: projects, clients, estimates, measurements and acts can be created offline and sync as soon as you're back online. The exception is photos — uploading and recognising them needs a connection.
landing.faqQ4: Can I export an estimate to PDF?
landing.faqA4: Yes. Both the estimate and the work-completion act can be opened or sent to the client as a PDF. On the PRO plan the PDF carries your logo.
landing.faqQ5: How is Majstr different from AVK-5?
landing.faqA5: AVK-5 is for state construction estimates under DSTU norms with resource-based pricing. Majstr is for private tradespeople and crews: market prices, a fast estimate for the client and a portal with online signing, without state norms.
landing.faqQ6: What's included in the free plan?
landing.faqA6: Two projects, up to three estimates per project, the client portal with online signing, PDF, photos, site measurements, project economy and work-completion acts. No card required.
landing.faqA7: Yes. An act is built from a signed estimate, and the client signs it online via a separate link; you can attach material receipts to it.

acts.advanceInfo: How much of the money already paid up front you credit against this act, so the client is not billed again for what they have already paid. Example: the client paid a 10 000 ₴ advance and this act is worth 15 000 ₴ — credit 10 000 ₴ and the client reads «Payable: 5 000 ₴». It is a DOCUMENT line: it changes «Payable» in the act, the PDF and the portal, but on its own it moves no figure in the object economy — that money is already counted there as «Received» and must not be counted twice. Leave it empty if the client pays for this act separately.

acts.shareTitle: Send the act to the client
acts.shareHint: The client can review the act and confirm acceptance of the works via the link.
acts.shareLegalInfo: Confirming via the link is a simple electronic form of consent, not a qualified electronic signature. A paper act or a QES is needed for indisputable legal force.
acts.whatIsInfo: A work-completion act is a document you and the client use to record which works are done and for how much. It's built from the positions of a signed estimate: tick what's completed and the act is ready. The client confirms acceptance via a link or on paper; once signed, the act is immutable. Interim acts close stages as the work progresses; a final act closes the whole object. Two important cautions: (1) additional works not in the estimate are safer agreed with the client BEFORE doing them — otherwise they have a legal right not to pay for them (art. 877 of the Civil Code). (2) A sole trader on group 2 cannot do work for a company on the general tax system — subcontracting for companies needs group 3.
acts.receiptsInfo: Materials or services you paid for yourself and re-bill to the client. No need to copy the receipt's line items — a label, an amount and a photo of the paper are enough (the photo is required: it is the proof). The receipts total is added to the act, and the client sees the receipts in the act portal and in the PDF.

acts.receiptsToExpensesInfo: Once the act is signed each receipt becomes an object expense (MATERIALS) so profit isn't inflated by money you merely passed through. Turn it off if you already log these receipts by hand.

shtroba.hint: Cable = bus + all drops (+ reserve). Chase = only what you actually cut. Millimetres.
shtroba.planHint: Draw the bus along the walls — we measure its length off the drawing. Drag the entry and the points.

electrical.title: Electrical plan
electrical.sourceHint: Upload a PDF or photo of the sockets/lighting plan — we count the points from its legend.
electrical.reviewHint: Check the counts against the plan. The model only counts points and reads heights — the calculator does the metres.
electrical.ledHint: The plan has LED strip. Add its metres by hand — a length off a drawing is not measured.
electrical.nothing: Could not read the plan. Try a clearer photo or the PDF.
electrical.applyHint: The points go into the chase/cable calculator — set the bus and what to chase there.
electrical.sectionHint: Electrical measurements: points from a plan + chase/cable calculator
electrical.pdfPages: PDF has {{count}} pages. Which are the socket/lighting plan? (e.g. 3 or 3-4)

portal.noSignedEstimates: No signed estimates yet — they'll appear here as soon as one is signed.

projectImport.title: Project documentation import
projectImport.sourceHint: Drop the designer’s folder as is: a zip archive, several PDFs or drawing photos. The useful sheets are picked out automatically.
projectImport.nothingUseful: No PDFs or photos found in the selection
projectImport.filesHint: Will recognise {{n}} of {{m}} files. Ticks are editable — add a missed one or untick noise.
projectImport.heightsHint: No ceiling height found in the drawings. Enter one per floor — walls can’t be computed without it (leave blank to skip).
projectImport.heightsSkipHint: Blank floor = no walls created, only floor/ceiling/skirting
projectImport.nothing: Nothing recognised. Try other sheets — a room schedule, measure plan or coverings spec.
projectImport.crossCheck: ⚠️ Room sum {{sum}} m² doesn’t match the schedule total {{total}} m² — some rooms were likely missed. Check the list.
projectImport.honesty: Project data is a high-quality draft, not a substitute for a tape measure. Designers themselves write “verify on site”.
projectImport.coveringsHint: Reference quantities from the project, not tied to rooms. Ticked ones are added as a separate group.
projectImport.needOnline: Recognition needs the internet. Try again when you are back online.
projectImport.archiveTooLarge: Archive is too large (up to 100 MB). Unpack it and send individual PDFs.
projectImport.sevenZipFailed: Could not unpack the 7z. Unpack the archive and drop the PDFs (several are fine), or re-pack as .zip.
projectImport.tooManySelected: Too many pages at once — pick up to {{max}}. Recognise the rest in another run.
projectImport.takeAllAreas: 📥 Take floor areas from the document ({{n}})
projectImport.makeCeilings: Create a ceiling for every room
projectImport.ceilingsHint: A separate ceiling mostly matters on a mansard with several planes. For a rectangular room it duplicates the floor.
projectImport.wallsNoHeight: Walls not computed: no height for “{{floor}}” — enter the height and re-run the import, or add walls manually
projectImport.canFull: The selected files will give: floor, walls (with a height), skirting, reveals.
projectImport.canAreas: The selected files will give: rooms with areas (floor). Add a measure plan for walls and skirting.
projectImport.coveringsOnly: ⚠️ A coverings spec gives ONLY areas — no sizes or walls will come out of it. Add a measure plan to compute walls, skirting and reveals.

el.areaTaken: Area taken from the document: {{area}} m²
el.areaHint: The document gives {{area}} m² — no sizes.

coverage.title: Recognised {{n}} rooms
coverage.mismatched: ⚠️ In {{n}} rooms the sizes were read but do not match the area — check below and decide whether to use them.

projectImport.rejectedHint: Read from the drawing: {{w}}×{{l}} m — does not match the {{area}} m² area, so it was not used.
projectImport.heightsFound: For {{n}} rooms the height came from the drawing (H=…) — only the rest are asked about.
projectImport.coveringsSkipped: The coverings spec is skipped — it gives no per-room measurements (only material totals).
projectImport.evidenceRaster: no text layer — recognisable only as an image
projectImport.guessedByEvidence: No sheet matched by name or stamp — ticked the ones that show data. Check the ticks.
projectImport.recheckHint: Highlighted figures were read from the drawing but not confirmed — measure on site and correct.
projectImport.triaging: Working out what these sheets are…
projectImport.triagingHint: One cheap call for the whole set, so nothing useless is read
